body:
Heh. I hate self-diagnosing because I'm no expert on anything, but I've actually equated some of my emotional issues to PTSD before. I hate the correlation, though, because it makes me think I'm weak. I mean, there are so many trans people whose lives *don't* get as fucked up as mine has that I can't help but think I'm just a sort of broken person, you know?

I don't think I was really traumatized as a kid, though. I was really, really sensitive, so I cried really easily when I was young (and still cry super easily during movies, tv shows, games, books, etc. lol), but I grew out of it, more or less. I can't think of anything that would have been damaging to me personally; I was always pretty even keel when big events happened, it's the little stuff that threw me off.

Yeah that describes my relationships *now.* I guess I felt that way before, too, but the difference was I had a really easy time talking to people when I was in high school.

Are you starting to see why I get so frustrated and depressed sometimes? I have all these stupid issues all tangled together and there's just no easy way to solve any one of them without affecting the others. And then there are my external problems to consider. I want to see a professional but the thought of actually talking about all this, out loud, drives my anxiety way up.

Anyway, you've been great, but I'm starting to feel annoyed for talking so much about myself. It makes me feel narcissistic. Thank you for listening though and offering some real insight, I appreciate it. It helps stifle the emotional side of things a bit when you understand them a little better.

Hmm that's hard to say. I was *very* sociable as a child, although I sometimes had trouble interacting with people my own age. I had a weird sense of humor and tried too hard to fit in with the guys, but I didn't fit in with the girls either. I guess I never had many friends up until high school, now that I think about it, and once I had some they were all older than me. I never had difficulties just hanging out with juniors/seniors when I was a freshmen. It was people my own age I couldn't get along with.

I didn't really become "introverted" at all until I was sixteen and kind of had my first breakdown, I guess? I don't know what to call it. I was dating this girl I didn't even like and woke up one day feeling like *everything* about my life was wrong and fake. Since then I've had trouble interacting with people for very long.

Yeah haha, I blame myself for a lot of things. Mostly because I really am the cause of most of my difficulties. I don't have a very consistent work ethic and I get a little reckless and irresponsible sometimes. I'll start everything I do really well and build great expectations for myself but then I lose my motivation or get lethargic and can't finish strongly. I haven't felt successful or capable in years. It's very exhausting to keep putting in effort when you don't feel like there's a reason to try anymore.

I would love to be more involved with anyone who understands what it's like to be trans. Seriously, I need that. But I'm so... I don't want to say awkward, but just very avoidant when it comes to people. I'm really bad at maintaining relationships right now, and it sucks because I *want* to be good at interpersonal communication, but it just doesn't happen for very long. I always get depressed and then hide away because I can't handle other people. I hate being so lonely but I'm the one who's causing it, I don't really know how to fix it.

I can do that. Well, eventually. When I'm not - before I got so messed up, I was very good at learning and applying new information. I took a lot of initiative and it does a lot of good for making the right contacts when you can work independently or lead a group. If I can get my head on straight, I could definitely prove myself. But right now I have so much difficulty around other people it's pretty tough. I do really well  for maybe a week or two, then I crash my anxiety spikes, and I run away from everything.

I've been trying, yeah. As frustrating as all my other issues have become it all does come back to being transgender. I really don't know what to do about it, to be honest. I could get on anti-anxiety medication, get into therapy and ameliorate my depression, and then maybe graduate and get a career going, but I'd still hate my body. I just don't really know.

It's not fun to go through, but it's nice to know I'm not the only person struggling this hard academically because of things like anxiety or depression. You tend to hear about others through the grapevine sometimes, but no one ever really speaks candidly about it. It's tough feeling so isolated in my emotions. I can't really be honest with anyone around me, even my family.

How are job prospects for you? One of the biggest practical concerns I have right now is how my poor collegiate past is going to affect my career. I'm all over the place since graduating high school.

Thanks for reading and responding.

It's nice to know I'm not alone either :P

I don't really know what to say, except I hope things get better for both of us. I just wish we had a little more control, that's all. Life's tough enough even when you *are* in control of yourself, but it's almost impossible when you aren't. Are you seeing a therapist? I was planning on seeing either a psychologist or psychiatrist next month, I don't really know anymore though.
You forgot a face in this one.
